name: Sweet Home 3D
tagline: Desktop app for drawing a floor plan in 2D and walking through it in 3D, with a furniture catalog.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified. The desktop app is free and open source under the GPL; paid options have historically included app store builds, an online version and extra furniture and texture packs.

verdictSummary: An agent can absolutely give you a 2D wall drawing tool with snapping and a crude extruded 3D preview in a weekend, and that part is genuinely satisfying. What it cannot give you is the rest of the product: a geometry kernel that handles sloped walls, levels, stairs, doors that cut openings correctly, plus thousands of modeled furniture pieces with real dimensions, plus a raytracer that makes a render you would show anyone. Those are years of work and licensed or contributed 3D content, not an afternoon of prompting. The punchline is that the desktop app is free and open source, so replacing it buys you nothing except a worse version of a thing you already have. Build the toy planner because it is fun, not because it saves money.
coreLoopDIY: Draw walls on a snapping grid, drop sized furniture boxes into rooms, and see the whole thing extruded into a walkable 3D view, all saved locally as JSON.
requirements: your own furniture dimensions, since you will be placing labeled boxes not models
whatYouLose: The furniture and texture catalog: thousands of real models with correct dimensions and materials
Photorealistic rendering, the raytraced stills and video walkthroughs
Correct architectural geometry: multiple levels, sloped ceilings, stairs, doors and windows that actually cut wall openings
Import and export in formats other people use, OBJ, DAE, SH3D, PDF plan printouts to scale
Twenty years of bug fixing in the parts that look easy, wall joins, dimension lines, undo
moatNotes: The catalog is the product. A floor planner without furniture models is graph paper with extra steps.
whyPeopleStillPay: Mostly they do not, because the core app is free. The money that does change hands goes to convenience and content: an app store build that auto updates, the browser version so you do not install Java, and furniture and texture packs so your kitchen has an actual dishwasher instead of a grey cuboid labeled dishwasher. That is a fair trade for a few euros and no coding agent shortens it.
notes: Replacing a free GPL desktop app with a weaker weekend clone is a hobby, not a saving. The moat is the furniture catalog and two decades of fiddly architectural geometry, and the fact that the real thing already costs nothing.
prompt:
Build a local, single-page floor planner called "Plan" in an empty folder. No accounts, no backend, no telemetry, no cloud.

Stack, non negotiable: Vite + TypeScript, three.js for the 3D view, plain Canvas 2D for the plan editor, zero UI framework. Persist to localStorage and support JSON file import/export.

Layout: left toolbar, center 2D plan canvas, right inspector panel, and a bottom toggle that swaps the center pane to the 3D view.

2D plan editor requirements:
- Grid in centimeters with configurable spacing, default 10cm, zoom with wheel, pan with space drag.
- Wall tool: click to place points, walls are polylines with thickness and height, snap to grid and to existing wall endpoints, escape to finish.
- Select tool: click a wall to edit thickness, height and length in the inspector, drag endpoints to move them.
- Furniture tool: place axis aligned rectangles from a small hardcoded list of about 12 items with real default sizes, bed, sofa, table, chair, fridge, counter, wardrobe, desk, toilet, sink, bathtub, door opening. Each item has width, depth, height, rotation and a color.
- Rotate selected furniture with R in 15 degree steps, delete with Delete, duplicate with Ctrl+D.
- Dimension display: show wall length in cm next to each wall while drawing and when selected.
- Full undo/redo via a simple command stack, Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Shift+Z.

3D view requirements:
- Extrude walls from the 2D data into boxes, render furniture as labeled boxes with their colors, add a floor plane sized to the plan bounds.
- OrbitControls, a hemisphere light plus one directional light, no shadows needed.
- Regenerate the scene from the model on every entry into 3D, do not try to keep two sources of truth.

Explicitly out of scope: multiple levels, sloped roofs, stairs, real openings cut into walls, textures, imported 3D models, raytraced rendering, PDF export, collaboration.

Deliver a README with run instructions, a src/model.ts holding the plan data types and pure geometry helpers, and Vitest unit tests for wall snapping, length computation and undo/redo. Keep total code under about 1500 lines and commit nothing that needs an API key or a .env file, because this app needs neither.
